tagline: Up Belt Creek through the silver camps and over the pass.
intro: From US 87 near Armington, US 89 turns south into the Little Belt Mountains and the Lewis and Clark National Forest, up the Belt Creek canyon through Monarch and Neihart and over Kings Hill Pass at 7,393 feet, then down toward White Sulphur Springs and US 12, 71 miles in all. Gravel roads branch off on both sides to lakes, trailheads and old mines.
Mining built the towns. The claims around Monarch went by King, Czar, Emperor, Rex and Sultan, and the Montana Central Railway reached Monarch from Great Falls in 1889.

moments.title: Sluice Boxes State Park
moments.text: Belt Creek winds the last eight miles out of the mountains between cliffs and ledges, past the leavings of the mining and railroad days.

moments.title: Neihart
moments.text: Three prospectors struck silver here in 1881. About $16 million in silver came out by 1929, and some 43 people live here now, at 5,661 feet.

moments.title: Kings Hill Pass
moments.text: The top of the road at 7,393 feet, with an observation tower over the national forest and Showdown's ski runs just to the south.

practical: Snow crews keep the pass open through the winter, but Visit Montana warns that winter driving can be difficult and advises checking road conditions.
